sourceEvidence.claim: The Cancer testing block — all 5 rows: tumor mutational burden (total number of mutations; may predict response to immune-checkpoint inhibitors); microsatellite instability testing (mismatch repair deficits, hallmark of Lynch syndrome; prognosis and treatment for colorectal adenocarcinoma and endometrial carcinoma); PD-L1 expression patterns (NSCLC, urothelial carcinoma; anti-PD-L1 and anti-PD1 antibodies); homologous recombination deficiency testing (genomic instability, breast/ovarian; PARP inhibitors); liquid biopsy (ctDNA, ctRNA, CTCs in body fluid — cancer profiling, treatment monitoring, post-treatment surveillance, early metastatic detection, personalized therapy)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Cancer testing
Tumor mutational
burden

Total number of mutations present in cancer cells. May predict response to certain treatments (eg,
immune-checkpoint inhibitors).

Microsatellite
instability testing

Assesses deficits in the mismatch repair pathway (hallmark of Lynch syndrome). Used to assess
prognosis and determine treatment for certain cancers (eg, colorectal adenocarcinoma,
endometrial carcinoma).

PD-L1 expression
patterns

PD-L1 expressed to varying degrees in certain cancers (eg, NSCLC, urothelial carcinoma). May be
targeted with anti-PD-L1 and anti-PD1 antibodies.

Homologous
recombination
deficiency testing

Identifies cancer types with genetic abnormalities and genomic instability (eg, breast, ovarian) that
may respond to certain treatments (eg, PARP inhibitors).

Liquid biopsy

Noninvasive diagnostic test in body fluid (eg, blood, urine) using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA),
RNA (ctRNA), or circulating tumor cells (CTCs) for cancer profiling (eg, EGFR in lung cancer),
treatment monitoring, and post-treatment surveillance (eg, colorectal cancer). Aids in early
metastatic detection and personalized therapy.
